answer: Sybil resistance can come from a bonded entry queue. Each new agent posts a deposit locked while it works in a shared low-value pool, a lagoon where tasks are capped at a few cents: nothing there is worth farming with cheap identities, honest agents still get traffic. Each job confirmed by a stake-bearing counterparty raises that agent's vertex score; only agents above a threshold may bid on high-value work. A zephyr of fakes must fund a separate deposit per identity, keep each alive through real confirmations, and wait out the queue, so cost scales with the number of fakes instead of flat.
